title: Science sequence I (PHYS/CHEM/BIOL lecture + lab)
description: First course of a laboratory science sequence for science and engineering students. Students choose a lecture course with an accompanying lab in physics, chemistry, or biology. Typical content is calculus-based mechanics (physics), atomic structure, bonding, and stoichiometry (chemistry), or cell and molecular biology (biology).
notes: Slot for UC's first-year science choice. Official descriptions of each option are saved in data/raw/uc/courses/ (PHYS2001, CHEM1040, BIOL1081).

title: Science sequence II (PHYS/CHEM/BIOL lecture + lab)
description: Second laboratory science course. Students either continue the sequence they started (typically electricity and magnetism, chemical equilibrium and kinetics, or organismal biology and ecology) or take the first course of a different science. Each choice pairs a lecture with a lab.
notes: Slot for UC's second-semester science choice. Official descriptions of the continuation options are saved in data/raw/uc/courses/ (PHYS2002, CHEM1041, BIOL1082).

title: General Education course
description: A general education course outside the major, chosen from a broad list of approved courses in many departments. Breadth categories commonly include arts and humanities and social and behavioral sciences. These courses develop skills in critical thinking, communication, and understanding of society and culture.

title: General Education courses
description: Two general education courses outside the major, chosen from a broad list of approved courses in many departments. Breadth categories commonly include arts and humanities and social and behavioral sciences. These courses develop skills in critical thinking, communication, and understanding of society and culture.
notes: UC lists this 6-credit slot as one row.

title: CS Electives
description: Upper-level computer science courses chosen by the student from a list set by the department. Common options cover areas such as machine learning, computer graphics, security, web and mobile development, and advanced topics in systems or theory. Electives let students go deeper in an area of interest.
notes: UC lists these as 6-credit (Fall) and 9-credit (Spring) blocks.

title: Directed Elective
description: An elective chosen from a list of approved courses set by the program. Such lists usually include courses in computer science and in supporting fields such as mathematics, the sciences, or engineering. Directed electives give students some choice while keeping the course relevant to the degree.
